sources_and_data.source: Reidl-Wahlstrom, Parameterized Algorithms for Zero Extension and Metric Labelling Problems
sources_and_data.use: exact metric-labeling objective, crossing-budget preservation target, and general O(k^(s+1)) baseline
prior-art boundary: tree vertex flow/cut sparsification is a different preservation object
source-matched definition and unrestricted novelty boundaries

method.type: direct proof with independent adversarial review; no experiment
method.host_class: finite connected standard cactus graphs, allowing a multigraph representation of two-edge cycle blocks
method.quantifiers: all finite metrics with |D|<=s, all injective terminal labelings, all integers k>=0
method.local_lemma: suppress internally vertex-disjoint paths with distinct endpoints and nonterminal degree-two interiors
method.global_reduction: prune terminal-free pendant block-cut subtrees, compress unmarked degree-two block-cut corridors, and suppress each cycle arc between boundary vertices
method.series_lemma: a series of unit edge bundles with multiplicities q_i in {1,2} is replaced by min_i(q_i) parallel edges
method.simple_output: replace each two-parallel-edge bundle by two internally vertex-disjoint length-two paths

mathematical_claim: For every finite connected standard cactus G with terminal set S, an exact k-bounded metric-labeling sparsifier H of O(|S|) edges exists for every admissible metric and injective terminal labeling; the k-exponent is 0. The theorem is exact in the multigraph model and has a simple fresh-vertex realization.
assumptions: The host cactus is finite, connected, unweighted, and each cycle block has the standard cactus property; a two-edge cycle is represented by two distinct parallel edges when needed.
The objective counts edge multiplicity separately and uses the same metric on every edge.
The sparsifier must preserve the exact restricted optimum, not a flow, cut, or approximation objective.
Fresh nonterminal vertices are allowed for the simple 4-cycle realization; if output must be a contraction on the original vertex set, only the multigraph-core statement is claimed.
verified_steps: The general local path-suppression lemma preserves cost and crossing count in both directions and does not require an acyclic host.
A pendant component attached through one vertex can be deleted by constant labeling, including loops and cycles attached at a terminal articulation.
A terminal-free series corridor of bridge/cycle bundles compresses exactly to a bundle of minimum multiplicity by triangle inequality and a minimum-weight label switch.
The block-cut tree reduction leaves only O(|S|) marked/branching nodes and O(|S|) cycle boundary arcs after degree-two corridors are compressed.
Cycles with two boundary vertices retain two independent arcs; cycles with three or more retain every boundary arc; zero/one-boundary blocks are removable under the stated terminal conditions.
Two parallel edges are exactly simulated by two internally disjoint length-two paths, so the earlier simple-output obstruction is refuted.
uncertainty: The theorem is restricted to standard connected cactus hosts and the explicit output conventions.
A contraction-only output on the original vertex set is a separate representation restriction.
No conclusion for unrestricted graphs or any lower bound follows.

proof_status.scope: standard connected cactus hosts with the explicit output conventions above
excluded_claims: No universal label-independent exponent theorem for unrestricted graphs.
No lower bound for arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers.
No claim that the result is publication-level novelty; the reductions are elementary and adjacent tree sparsification is known prior art.

independent_review.review_type: adversarial proof review of path, pendant, cycle, series, and representation cases
reviewed_failure_modes: cycles incorrectly treated as blocking local path compression
parallel edges incorrectly treated as impossible to simulate simply
terminal-free cycle chains with degree-four articulations
terminal articulations, loops, and one-boundary cycles
hidden s-dependent size or k exponent
independent_review.review_conclusion: The multigraph cactus theorem and its simple fresh-vertex realization are closed; contraction-only simple-output restrictions remain a separate representation condition, not a mathematical obstruction to the stated sparsifier model.

observed_result_or_blocker.result: Complete exact cactus restriction theorem with O(|S|) edges and universal k-exponent 0.
observed_result_or_blocker.prior_art_boundary: The reductions are standard and not claimed as a new breakthrough; Goranci-Raecke addresses flow/cut vertex sparsifiers rather than this metric-labeling objective.
observed_result_or_blocker.next_obstacle: O7 contraction-only distinguishable metric-signature lower-bound construction, followed by the harder lift to arbitrary sparsifiers.
negative_findings: The previous simple-output obstruction was false because a 4-cycle gadget preserves two parallel edge signatures exactly.
No asymptotic lower bound follows from this restricted theorem.

paper3_state_check: Paper 3 Target A and Target B unchanged; no forecast or evidence label edited.
next_falsifiable_action: Develop the O7 contraction-only lower-bound family without executing an experiment; prove pairwise metric-cost separation and separately test whether any conclusion can transfer to arbitrary terminal-preserving sparsifiers.
